cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Appreciating every day – The core thematic concept of appreciating every day as explored and highlighted in 'About Time'.

p.em: Example: The narrative of 'About Time' brilliantly dissects appreciating every day to build character depth as Tim Lake confronts using secret time travel to master daily appreciation and father-son bonds.

cosy-blockquote.p: time travel – The core thematic concept of time travel as explored and highlighted in 'About Time'.

p.em: Example: The narrative of 'About Time' brilliantly dissects time travel to build character depth as Tim Lake confronts using secret time travel to master daily appreciation and father-son bonds.

cosy-blockquote.p: father-son bond – The core thematic concept of father-son bond as explored and highlighted in 'About Time'.

p.em: Example: The narrative of 'About Time' brilliantly dissects father-son bond to build character depth as Tim Lake confronts using secret time travel to master daily appreciation and father-son bonds.

cosy-blockquote.p: Redemption – The core thematic concept of redemption as explored and highlighted in 'About Time'.

p.em: Example: The narrative of 'About Time' brilliantly dissects redemption to build character depth as Tim Lake confronts using secret time travel to master daily appreciation and father-son bonds.

cosy-blockquote.p: Deception ≠ Honesty – the action of deceiving someone ≠ the quality of being honest and truthful.

p.em: Example: A web of deception was uncovered, contrasting sharply with her lifelong dedication to honesty.

cosy-blockquote.p: Bloke – (noun) an informal British term for a man.

p.em: Example: Tim's father affectionately refers to everyday people as a 'bloke' while giving timeless life advice.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
When we first enter the world of Cornwall and bustling London, how does the opening scene establish tension through appreciating every day? Integrate unreal Past & Regrets (*wish / if only*).
★ If you were placed in Cornwall and bustling London, how would you personally handle the challenges of appreciating every day?

How does the director introduce the theme of time travel early in 'About Time' to set the atmospheric tone? Focus on unreal Past & Regrets (*wish / if only*).
★ Have you ever faced a dilemma where you had to prioritize time travel over your relationship with someone like his father, Mary, and his quirky British family?

As the narrative progresses, how do the rising anxieties of Tim Lake regarding father-son bond complicate their relationship with his father, Mary, and his quirky British family? Frame using unreal Past & Regrets (*wish / if only*).
★ Does the cinematic portrayal of father-son bond in 'About Time' match your own experiences in the real world?

How do the quiet scenes in Cornwall and bustling London reveal a hidden friction of redemption between Tim Lake and his father, Mary, and his quirky British family? Use unreal Past & Regrets (*wish / if only*).
★ What is your personal strategy for keeping redemption in balance when facing stressful situations?

What psychological defense mechanisms does Tim Lake use when coping with the harsh reality of deception? Discuss using unreal Past & Regrets (*wish / if only*).
★ If you had the opportunity to change one choice made by Tim Lake regarding deception, what would it be?

Which subtle narrative clues and secrets about 'bloke' are hidden from us in Cornwall and bustling London? How would you express your deduction using unreal Past & Regrets (*wish / if only*) (e.g., examining light, framing, or pacing choices)?
★ Have you ever used a slang term or colloquial expression like 'bloke' in your own life? Tell us about it.

How does the screenplay use the expression 'fancy' during a crucial turning point to accelerate the suspense? Respond with unreal Past & Regrets (*wish / if only*).
★ Do you think learning informal slang like 'fancy' is essential for fluency, or do you prefer formal language?

How does the characters' usage of 'shambles' reveal their true motives and lies during using secret time travel to master daily appreciation and father-son bonds? Formulate with unreal Past & Regrets (*wish / if only*).
★ Is there an equivalent idiom in your native language for the expression 'shambles'? How does it compare?

How does the final revelation of 'dry run' change the audience's entire understanding of the characters' actions? Analyze utilizing unreal Past & Regrets (*wish / if only*).
★ When you want to express a complex feeling, do you rely on direct words or colloquial markers like 'dry run'?

If Tim Lake had accepted the truth about 'tonal shift' earlier in 'About Time', how would the ending have changed? Speculate using unreal Past & Regrets (*wish / if only*).
★ What is your favorite piece of informal dialogue from 'About Time', and why does it stick with you?

cosy-blockquote.p: Compare the adaptation differences and visual contrasts in About Time. - 🎬Original Screenplay Adaptations - 🎭Visual Directing & Setting Contrasts

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Look at the prompt and discuss your response with your teacher:

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
'Tim Lake's story of appreciating every day in 'About Time' is very sad, and they should be more careful.' Do you agree? Use unreal Past & Regrets (*wish / if only*).
★ If you were a director, how would you visually represent the abstract concept of appreciating every day?

'Tim Lake's movie makes the world of Cornwall and bustling London look too beautiful, but it has a high cost.' Discuss using unreal Past & Regrets (*wish / if only*).
★ Do you agree that the visual environment of a film is more powerful than its written dialogue?

'Tim Lake is not a nice person because they only care about father-son bond.' Give your opinion using unreal Past & Regrets (*wish / if only*).
★ Have you ever felt that a movie's alternative ending would have been more meaningful than the actual one?

'Tim Lake's movie 'About Time' is too simple and does not show deep feelings about redemption.' Talk about this with unreal Past & Regrets (*wish / if only*).
★ If you had to select a soundtrack from your own life to match the theme of redemption, what would it be?

'Tim Lake's problem of using secret time travel to master daily appreciation and father-son bonds never ends because they cannot agree on deception.' Explain using unreal Past & Regrets (*wish / if only*).
★ What was the most visually striking scene in 'About Time' that made you pause and reflect?

'The film would have achieved a far more powerful dramatic effect if the director had chosen a completely different setting for 'About Time'.' Speculate using unreal Past & Regrets (*wish / if only*).
★ Would you ever want to write a screenplay based on your own life experiences? Why or why not?

'The secondary characters, particularly his father, Mary, and his quirky British family, are far more interesting and complex than the main protagonist.' Evaluate with unreal Past & Regrets (*wish / if only*).
★ Which cinematic technique (lighting, music, camera angles) do you find has the most visceral impact on your emotions?

'The music and sound design (or the absolute use of silence) are what make 'About Time' a cinematic masterpiece.' Discuss using unreal Past & Regrets (*wish / if only*).
★ If you were casting a remake of 'About Time', which modern actors would you choose for Tim Lake?

'The recursive visual motifs (like locked doors, fog, or recurring colors) are essential to understanding the film's deeper meaning.' Critique using unreal Past & Regrets (*wish / if only*).
★ Do you enjoy analyzing films on a technical level, or do you prefer to just enjoy the story?

'The screenplay of 'About Time' is ultimately a critique of real-world human behavior rather than just an entertaining genre film.' Argue your thesis using unreal Past & Regrets (*wish / if only*).
★ If you could preserve only one scene from 'About Time' for future generations, which one would it be?

ul.li: Incorrect: Seldom I have seen such an ending → Correct: Seldom have I seen such an ending (Negative adverbs like 'seldom' at the beginning of a clause trigger subject-auxiliary inversion.)
Incorrect: If they would have warned us, we would know → Correct: If they had warned us, we would know (Use past perfect (had + past participle) in the if-clause of a mixed conditional.)
Incorrect: He insisted she goes to Runway → Correct: He insisted she go to Runway (Verbs of demand/insistence like 'insist' trigger the subjunctive/bare infinitive.)
